origin.description: Estimation of scale based on sequential-order differences, corresponding to the scale estimates provided by stats::var, stats::sd, stats::mad and stats::IQR.
origin.usage:
madDiff(x, idxs = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, diff = 1L, trim = 0,
  constant = 1.4826, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length N or a numeric N by K matrix.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.text: The positional distance of elements for which the difference should be calculated.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: A double in [0, 1/2] specifying the fraction of observations to be trimmed from each end of the sorted values before estimation.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: A scale factor adjusting for asymptotically normal consistency.

origin.details: n-order difference MAD estimates, like stats::mad, apply a consistency factor for the Gaussian standard deviation. The IQR estimates do not. That factor would be 1 / (2 * qnorm(3/4)) and has to be applied by hand. Differences are computed by diff2, which is a faster diff. The result is then divided by 2^diff for the variance and by sqrt(2)^diff otherwise. The divisor uses the original diff, while diff2 truncates the order with as.integer.

translation.description: Estimation of scale based on sequential-order differences, corresponding to the scale estimates provided by stats::var, stats::sd, stats::mad and stats::IQR.
translation.usage:
madDiff(x, idxs=None, na_rm=False, diff=1, trim=0,
  constant=1.4826, low=False, high=False, center=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector, or a matrix read in column-major order. Integer NA, the value -2147483648, is missing. Logical values are accepted when diff is 0.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based indexes, or None for every element. This is idxs in R. Positive indexes select, zero is dropped, and a negative index drops that position. A missing or out-of-range positive index inserts a missing value. Logical indexes are recycled when shorter than x.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are dropped before the differences are formed. This is na.rm in R. The default is False.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.text: Order of difference passed to diff2, default 1. diff2 truncates a non-integer with as.integer. The scale correction still uses this original value, so 1.9 is a first difference divided by 2^1.9. Zero skips the difference. A negative value is an error.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Fraction trimmed from each end of the sorted differences before the scale estimate. The default is 0. The kept slice is lo:hi with lo = floor(n * trim) + 1 and hi = n + 1 - lo. A missing value in that slice makes the estimate missing when trim is positive.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: The consistency factor passed to the MAD, default 1.4826, the same default as stats::mad. It is applied before dividing by sqrt(2)^diff.

arguments.name: low
arguments.text: If True, and the number of deviations is even, return the lower of the two central absolute deviations instead of their mean. The default is False. This is forwarded to stats::mad.

arguments.name: high
arguments.text: If True, and the number of deviations is even, return the higher of the two central absolute deviations. The default is False. low and high cannot both be True.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Center for the absolute deviations. None uses the median, as stats::mad does.

translation.details: The calculation runs on the vector, or on the column-major contents of a matrix. Differences come from matrixstats.diff2.diff2, with lag 1. The estimate is stats::mad with the given constant, divided by sqrt(2)^diff. stats::var is the compensated two-pass sample variance. stats::sd is its square root. stats::mad is constant times the median absolute deviation from the median, default constant 1.4826. The quartiles follow stats::quantile, default type 7. low, high, and center are forwarded to the MAD. low and high pick one central deviation when the count is even. center replaces the default median. Integer input is read as float64, and R's integer NA becomes a missing value before diff2.
translation.value: A Python float. Missing results are nan.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.vardiff import madDiff

madDiff(np.array([1.0, 3.0, 6.0, 10.0]))
